analysis.title: F'ed: MegaCaps Maul Markets After Warsh's Waffling Waves Off Higher Oil
key_insights: The Fed held rates at the Oct 28-29 meeting with 2 dissents, fewer than expected, and Lisa Cook joined the dissenters. The statement added a commitment to 'accumulate more information'.

Warsh rejected signaling policy decisions or prejudging meetings in the presser. He was positive on employment and hawkish on inflation, which has run above the committee's objective for close to six years.
Warsh said financial conditions are tighter but he is unwilling and unable to call them tight. He framed the tightening as supporting a longer, more durable period of growth and price stability.
In 2027 one Fed meeting will focus on broad monetary policy strategy with no policy vote, so there will be seven rate decisions instead of eight. In 2028 there will be six.

UBS reads the new wording about accumulating more data as a nod to Warsh basing decisions on trends rather than single data points. If trends continue, a December hike is on. December hike odds stayed high and January odds fell during the presser.

Rate-hike expectations dipped slightly, with 2027 the most volatile during the presser. The curve steepened, with short-end yields falling and long-end yields rising, and the 10Y yield moved back above 5.00% before closing back at 5.00%.

Oil rose near multi-month highs on WSJ-reported US planning for a short, intense post-Midterms campaign against Iran. Iran rejected a Qatar proposal to end the war, then said it continues to give diplomacy a chance, which knocked crude off its highs. WTI hit $103.50 intraday and was at about $102 after hours.
The Houthis claimed a ballistic missile strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery (550,000 b/d capacity). The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted three ballistic missiles and four drones.

US commercial crude stocks fell more than expected for a fourth straight weekly decline, and US crude exports hit nearly 5 million b/d, a record. The WTI Cash Roll remains dramatically elevated and Dated Brent ticked higher.

Oracle said it will limit additional capital raises to $20B for FY27-FY30, which lifted neoclouds, data centers and optical networking and compressed credit spreads, including data-center bond spreads.
SK Hynix's strong earnings lifted AI names. The broad AI basket is outperforming SPX ex-AI by 760bps this week, but Goldman traders said 'nobody is chasing'. SPX is within 1% of record highs.

Mag7 lagged ahead of earnings. After hours MSFT was up about 6% and GOOG down about 8%, with GOOGL at its lowest level since April. Nasdaq futures erased the day's gains, and Fortinet and ServiceNow also weighed.

Vanda Research says institutional options buying is recovering. Daily net call buying was well above its 1M moving average, particularly in AI themes, after a sharp slowdown the prior week. VIX fell all day into the MegaCap earnings, with a lot of vol priced in.
